| fr-0002 | 16 of builder/plan's 22 declared sections can never be created — the section set is frozen at scaffold time | hard-wall | pij-disturbing-ox | chainglass, dd-builder dogfood | builder/plan declares 22 sections; `harness plan new` scaffolds only 6 (meta, summary, goals, non_goals, acceptance_criteria, phases). The other 16 — testing_strategy, documentation_strategy, key_findings, gate_matrix, risks, risks_assumptions, open_questions, clarifications, planning_seam, acceptance_coverage, implementation_summary, execution_guardrails, research_context, workshop_opportunities, tasks, done_when — CANNOT BE CREATED. `dd set` and `dd add` both refuse with E450 section-unknown ('the document has no section X'), and there is no add-section verb: dd has get/set/add/rm, and `rm` can DELETE a section but nothing creates one. So the section set is frozen at scaffold time, permanently. | Hand-edit plan.dd.json then `harness dd build` — which the builder skill explicitly forbids ('never hand-edit plan.dd.json'), even though the dd README sanctions it. So the only escape route is one the calling skill prohibits. | Either `plan new` scaffolds every declared section empty, or set/add auto-create a schema-DECLARED section. Workaround used there was a structural JSON insert of empty sections followed immediately by plan validate + render to prove schema-validity and no drift. | The sharpest part of ox's report is the one I did not make: this DIRECTLY BREAKS /builder 1b plan, whose module instructs the agent to author key_findings, gate_matrix, clarifications, planning_seam, testing_strategy, risks and open_questions — none of which dd can hold. So a skill and a tool that ship together disagree about what is possible, and the only bridge between them is an action one of them forbids. E450's message is also arguably the real defect: 'the document has no section X' is TRUE and useless, because it describes the document when the actionable fact is whether the SCHEMA allows X. An error that names the wrong authority sends the reader to the wrong fix. |
